issues.description: Guard fires for all non-Tab keys and may not fully short-circuit the Enter-accept path
issues.detail: The new block sits inside the Enter/Return/Tab handler but only excludes Tab, so any non-Tab key reaching this code hides the popup and replays the event. The intended invariant -- 'Enter behaves as a normal keystroke when disabled' -- needs to be restated and narrowed explicitly to Return/Enter, with the downstream accept path confirmed dead.

issues.description: get_conf called on every keystroke in the completion popup hot path
issues.detail: Reading the config through the plugin conf system on every keyPressEvent is a dictionary walk per keystroke for a static user preference. Cache the value when the popup is shown or subscribe to option changes, and read from an attribute in the handler.

issues.description: Condition `not self.get_conf(...) and not key == Qt.Key_Tab` reads backwards
issues.detail: Bind the conf to a named local and rewrite as `if not enter_accepts and key != Qt.Key_Tab`. The double-negation and `not ==` form obscures intent in a keyPressEvent handler where readers cannot afford ambiguity. Trivial mechanical fix that makes the invariant self-evident.

issues.description: Special case bolted onto an overloaded keyPressEvent instead of restructuring the dispatch
issues.detail: Rather than wedging a guard mid-function after currentItem(), compute an 'is this key an accept key right now?' predicate at the top from config + key. The early-exit belongs with sibling key handlers, avoiding wasted currentItem() work and the awkward hide+replay dance.

issues.description: Replaying the event via textedit.keyPressEvent is fragile and may double-handle
issues.detail: Hiding the popup then forwarding to the underlying editor couples the popup to the editor's exact event semantics and could double-fire if Qt also propagates the unhandled event. Prefer event.ignore() and normal Qt propagation, or eat the event explicitly -- not both.

issues.description: No test coverage for the new disabled-Enter branch
issues.detail: Completion key handling regresses silently. A single test that toggles the preference off, sends Enter, and asserts no completion was accepted would prevent the next maintainer from undoing this by accident.

synthesis.summary: Small, scoped patch adding a 'use_enter_for_completions' preference that solves a real user problem with a correct default. The panel agrees it NEEDS-WORK on taste and hygiene: the guard is wedged inside an overloaded keyPressEvent as a special case rather than restructured as an accept-key predicate, the condition uses awkward `not ==` double-negation, and get_conf is called on every keystroke instead of cached. The Enter short-circuit invariant should be stated and narrowed explicitly to Return/Enter, and the event-replay dance is fragile. Fix the condition, cache the config, restructure the dispatch, and add a regression test -- then it lands.
